subject: physics
topicDisplay: Theme D · Fields (Gravitational, Electric & Magnetic, Motion in Fields)
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Gravitational field strength g is defined as:
questions.explain: g = F/m, measured in N/kg, equal to the acceleration of free fall.

questions.q: Newton's law of gravitation states the force between two masses is:
options: Proportional to the product of masses and inversely proportional to the square of their separation
questions.explain: F = G*M*m/r^2, an inverse-square law.

questions.q: If the distance between two masses is doubled, the gravitational force between them becomes:
questions.explain: Inverse-square law: force is proportional to 1/r^2, so doubling r gives 1/4 the force.

questions.q: Gravitational field lines around a point mass:
options: Point radially inward towards the mass
questions.explain: Field lines show the direction of force on a small test mass, towards the attracting mass.

questions.q: At the surface of the Earth, g is about 9.8 N/kg. This is numerically equal to the:
questions.explain: Field strength in N/kg equals free-fall acceleration in m/s^2.

questions.q: A satellite in a stable circular orbit is kept in orbit by:
questions.explain: Gravitational attraction supplies exactly the centripetal force for circular orbital motion.

questions.q: Electric field strength E is defined as:
questions.explain: E = F/q, measured in N/C or V/m.

questions.q: Coulomb's law describes the force between two point charges as:
options: Proportional to the product of charges and inversely proportional to separation squared
questions.explain: F = k*q1*q2/r^2, another inverse-square law.

questions.q: Two like charges placed near each other will:
questions.explain: Like charges repel; opposite charges attract.

questions.q: Electric field lines point:
questions.explain: By convention field lines show the force direction on a positive test charge.

questions.q: A uniform electric field exists between:
questions.explain: Parallel plates produce a uniform field with evenly spaced, parallel field lines.

questions.q: Magnetic field lines around a bar magnet run:
options: From the north pole to the south pole (outside the magnet)
questions.explain: Field lines emerge from the north pole and return to the south pole.

questions.q: A current-carrying wire produces a magnetic field that is:
questions.explain: Concentric circular field lines surround a straight current-carrying conductor.

questions.q: The force on a charge q moving at speed v perpendicular to a magnetic field B is:
questions.explain: The magnetic force on a moving charge is maximum when v is perpendicular to B.

questions.q: A charged particle enters a uniform magnetic field perpendicular to it. Its path is:
questions.explain: The magnetic force is always perpendicular to velocity, providing a centripetal force for circular motion.

questions.q: The force on a straight wire of length L carrying current I in a field B (perpendicular) is:
questions.explain: The motor effect force is greatest when the current is perpendicular to the field.

questions.q: A charged particle moving parallel to a magnetic field experiences a magnetic force of:
questions.explain: When v is parallel to B, the magnetic force qvB sin(theta) is zero (theta = 0).

questions.q: The direction of the force on a current-carrying wire in a magnetic field is given by:
questions.explain: Fleming's left-hand rule gives the motor-effect force direction (thrust, field, current).

questions.q: Both gravitational and electric (Coulomb) forces are inverse-square laws, but a key difference is that gravity is:
options: Always attractive, while electric force can attract or repel
questions.explain: Masses only attract; charges can attract or repel depending on sign.

questions.q: Doubling the speed of a charge moving perpendicular to a magnetic field doubles the:
questions.explain: F = qvB, so force is proportional to speed for fixed q and B.
